the NLRs of luminous obscured AGN are small (≲10 kpc) and that the NLR size–luminosity relationship flattens at luminous AGN luminosities.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the size of the [O III]-emitting region in luminous obscured quasar hosts is ~7 kpc, regardless of IR luminosity.
there is an upper limit to the size of the ionized NLR of luminous quasaries of ~10 kpc.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are two regimes of NLR size: one for objects with log (L 8μm/erg s−1) < 44.5 and one for objects with L 8μm > 10 45 erg s−1.
the NLR size is a function of both the AGN luminosity and a maximal physical extent.
the NLR size-luminosity relation is flat above a luminosity of ~1044.3 erg s–1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLR size-luminosity relation is not a simple power law, but rather is better described by a power law that flattens at a luminosity-dependent maximal size.
the NLR size-luminosity relationships are not linear, but rather have a maximum size.
NLR sizes are not directly proportional to the luminosity of the active galactic nucleus.
